data.narrative:
CuspAI is a Series A–stage AI & Software company founded by Max Welling and Chad Edwards that has raised over $100M to date. Valuation analysis draws on a peer universe of 9 comparable companies (1 public, 8 private) operating in the same sector and stage, including Scale AI, Reflection AI, Physical Intelligence, and Black Forest Labs.

Two triangulation methods were applied. The stage-progression approach uses the $100M total raised as a valuation proxy and applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier typical for Series A progression, yielding $200M. The peer-median method examines four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage comparables with valuations ranging from $3.2B (Black Forest Labs, Series B) to $29.0B (Scale AI, Series B), producing a median implied valuation of $15.3B. The wide peer range reflects substantial heterogeneity in AI & Software valuations even within adjacent funding stages.

The triangulated analysis supports a broad valuation range of $170M to $17.6B, with a median point of $7.8B. The significant spread reflects two distinct valuation regimes: the stage-progression method anchors to capital deployed, while the peer-median approach captures market-based pricing for later-stage AI software companies. The applicable range narrows materially if recent comparables (Reflection AI at $25.0B, Series A) receive lower weight due to potential market exuberance in high-profile AI rounds. Key uncertainties include CuspAI's revenue generation, unit economics, and proprietary technical defensibility relative to the peer set.
